texts.preamble: Gayam Venkateswara Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 30 December, 2019 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Rakesh Kumar
texts.arguments: 2. Two petitioners have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973 with a prayer to quash the First Information Report (F.I.R) i.e., F.I.R No.264 of 2019, registered on the file of Tenali III Town P.S., Guntur District, primarily on the ground that in similar circumstances this court has interfered and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the F.I.R. 3. A reliance has been placed on an unreported judgment, dated 18-12-2019, as passed in Criminal Petition No.5421 of 2019 and other connected cases and also a common order passed by a learned single Judge of this Court, dated 27.08.2018, in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and other connected petitions. 4. By way of placing F.I.R, learned counsel for the petitioners has argued that save except recovery of tobacco products, which are prohibited under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006,( for short "the Act") no other cognizable offence is made out. He submits that since in an identical situation, this court has interfered with the F.I.R and also during initial investigation, this court may pass similar order. 5. The learned Public Prosecutor has tried to persuade the court that if a cognizable offence under the provisions of IPC is made out along with the offences under the Act, the police is having jurisdiction to lodge F.I.R and investigate the same.
